// Must-trip fixture for the literal scan: a ".." comparison in a PATH context,
// which is the second containment implementation this phase exists to remove.
//
// Both shapes here are the ones that were actually in the tree — neither
// matches a marker set calibrated only on the post-fix source, so a regression
// reintroducing either has to go red on a fixture rather than on the live code
// it would be reintroduced into.
package scanfixture

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// containedPath as it stood in internal/cmd/security.go: filepath.Rel plus an
// os.PathSeparator-joined prefix test.
func containedPath(runDir, name string) (string, error) {
	p := filepath.Join(runDir, name)
	rel, err := filepath.Rel(runDir, p)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(os.PathSeparator)) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("path %q escapes the run directory", name)
	}
	return p, nil
}

// RunDir as it stood in internal/remote/remote.go: path.Base equality with a
// bare ".." arm.
func runDir(runID string) (string, error) {
	if runID != path.Base(runID) || runID == "." || runID == ".." {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("run id %q is not a single path segment", runID)
	}
	return path.Join(".dross-runs", runID), nil
}

// The testlane / verify shape: clean, then test the cleaned string.
func normalize(p string) (string, bool) {
	c := path.Clean(p)
	if c == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(c, "../") {
		return c, false
	}
	return c, true
}
